about: Validation of every hazard map GeoHUB publishes, against held-out historical events. Built by GeoID_GIS/services/hazard_metrics.py; methods in GeoID_GIS/docs/notes/hazards.md.

maps.name: Flood susceptibility — global (random forest, 0.1°)

model.method: Random forest on (cell, event) rows: terrain, land cover, soil and climate at the cell plus that event's rainfall; trained on Copernicus EMS flood delineations in six regions.

inputs.name: Historical floods

inputs.licence: Copernicus data: free, full and open, any use with attribution (© European Union, Copernicus Emergency Management Service)

inputs.name: Soil

inputs.licence: NASA ORNL DAAC: free to use with citation

inputs.name: Rainfall, climate and events
inputs.source: NOAA CPC Global Unified Gauge-Based daily precipitation, 0.5°

inputs.name: Rainfall, now
inputs.source: CPC realtime, as of 2026-10-21

validation.threshold_rule: per region: Youden's J on the out-of-bag votes of the forest trained on the OTHER regions
validation.holdout: leave one region out: 6 of 6 regions each scored by a forest that never saw it (142 EMS delineation products)
validation.events: Copernicus EMS: cells inside the observed flood extent = 1; cells analysed (area of interest ∩ image footprint, minus not-analysed and mapped water) and not flooded = 0

americas.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

asia.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

africa.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

mediterranean.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

europe-north-west.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

europe-central-east.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

validation.auc_rule: mean of the held-out regions' AUCs (each region's scores come from its own forest, so pooling them mixes calibrations; the pooled figure is auc_pooled)

current.rain: CPC realtime: wettest 3 days of the last 7, and the 30 before

limits: The open EMS API covers activations from 2023 on: 90 floods, three quarters in Europe. The Americas, Africa and Asia are each scored on a handful of activations, and their numbers carry that uncertainty.

Negatives are cells the analysts looked at and did not map as flooded. EMS areas of interest are drawn around the affected ground, so the dry cells sit beside the flood: harder to separate than random dry land, which makes AUC conservative -- and a mapper's omission (a flooded street under trees) is counted as dry.
Flood traces and flooded areas are both taken as flooded; modelled extents are not used.

Each activation is one region's rows; activations share rivers and mapping teams, which is why the hold-out is by REGION rather than by cell -- a random cell split would score near 0.99 and mean nothing.
Probabilities are relative (two dry cells per flooded one in training); the threshold turns them into a map.
Land cover is 2020 for every event.

The 0.1° map leans European: most training floods are, so European lowlands read redder than ground of the same shape elsewhere -- the Africa held-out AUC (0.58 at 0.1°) is the measure of how far that carries.
D8 on a 0.1° DEM draws parallel flow lines across very flat basins (the Congo, the Amazon floodplain): the streaks there are routing artefacts, not rivers.
Terrain at a window's edge sees no upstream area beyond it, so a big river entering a 1° window reads smaller than it is -- the same on the page, which uses the same window logic.

maps.name: Flood susceptibility — Wales (random forest on NRW records)
maps.product: data/global/flood-susceptibility-wales-current.tif — today's map; the NI prototype's weighted overlay (ni-flood.js) remains the in-browser screening map

model.method: Random forest classifier on (cell, event) pairs: static terrain, geology, land cover and climate at the cell plus that event's own rainfall; the output is the share of trees voting 'flooded'.

inputs.name: Historical floods
inputs.source: Natural Resources Wales, Historic Flood Map (OGL v3)
inputs.detail: 127 dated events used; excluded: {'before 1979-02': 175, '1 January placeholder': 8, 'undated': 0}

inputs.name: Satellite land cover
inputs.source: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 (Sentinel-1/2, CC BY 4.0)
inputs.detail: 10 m classes read at 33 m, as fractions per cell

inputs.name: Elevation
inputs.source: Terrarium DEM (AWS Open Data; SRTM/GMTED/OS Terrain), zoom 10
inputs.detail: slope, HAND, upstream area, channel distance, TWI, curvature derived here

inputs.name: Superficial geology
inputs.source: BGS Geology 625k (OGL; Contains British Geological Survey materials © UKRI)

inputs.name: Rainfall, climate
inputs.source: Met Office HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 annual normals (OGL)

inputs.name: Rainfall, past events
inputs.source: NOAA CPC Global Unified Gauge-Based Daily Precipitation, 0.5° (public domain)

inputs.name: Rainfall, now
inputs.source: Open-Meteo forecast API, the feed GeoHUB's Forecast panel reads

model.grid: 900 x 1050 cells of 0.003 x 0.002 deg (~204 x 221 m), Wales high-water-mark mask

elevation_m.method: none needed; seabed cells dropped from the mask
elevation_m.why: Terrarium has no voids over Wales; cells below -5 m inside the high-water mark are estuary bathymetry and are not modelled

slope_deg.why: the coastal ring where a central difference reaches the sea

curvature.why: the coastal ring where a central difference reaches the sea

twi.why: the coastal ring where a central difference reaches the sea

deposit_score.method: not a gap: no superficial unit means bedrock at surface, scored 0.2
deposit_score.why: the NI acceptance run lost two thirds of South Wales treating this as no-data

built_frac.why: WorldCover no-data pixels (none expected over land)

water_frac.why: WorldCover no-data pixels (none expected over land)

wetland_frac.why: WorldCover no-data pixels (none expected over land)

tree_frac.why: WorldCover no-data pixels (none expected over land)

crop_frac.why: WorldCover no-data pixels (none expected over land)

rain_normal_mm.method: inverse-distance weighting, power 2, 8 nearest 12 km cells
rain_normal_mm.why: HadUK-Grid's 12 km cells do not tile the coast or lakes (Lough Neagh and Slieve Donard came back empty in NI); every land cell is interpolated from 190 cell centres so none is left out

cpc_daily.method: inverse-distance weighting across that day's other half-degree cells
cpc_daily.why: a CPC cell with no gauge report on a day

validation.threshold_rule: Youden's J on the TRAINING events' out-of-bag predictions, fixed before the test set was scored
validation.holdout: temporal: trained on 37 events before 2005, scored on 72 events from 2005 to 2025
validation.events: NRW Historic Flood Map outlines (cells inside an event's outline = 1; cells of Wales outside it on the same dates = 0, two per positive and at least 500 per event)

limits: An outline's absence is not a dry record: NRW maps the floods it knows of, so some negatives were wet.
Event rainfall is a 0.5° gauge analysis; a convective storm smaller than a cell is smoothed away.
Repeat floods in the same towns put correlated cells in train and test; the temporal split keeps the events apart, not the places.

The hold-out tests WHERE a storm floods, not WHETHER: each event's dry cells share its rain, so rainfall barely moves the held-out AUC (see auc_without_rainfall). How the map responds to today's rain is the forest's learnt between-event contrast and is not separately validated here.
Negatives run at least 500 per event, so small events carry many more than two per positive; accuracy and specificity are read at that mix (positives/negatives on the card).
Probabilities are relative (two negatives per positive in training), not annual chances; the decision threshold is what turns them into a map.
Trained on Wales; transfer elsewhere (the NI prototype area) is an extrapolation of the same recipe, as the landslide recipe's South Wales validation was.

maps.name: Landslide susceptibility — global preview (random forest, 0.1°)

model.method: Random forest on terrain (slope, relief, curvature, HAND, TWI, upstream area), GLiM lithology, Sentinel-2 land cover, soil thickness and the rain climate, trained on inventoried landslides; replaces Recipe A's weighted overlay.

parameters.absence_rule: ≥3 cells (~30 km) from any slide, within ~1° of a report
parameters.positive_rule: NASA catalogue slides located within 5 km (BGS kept out: see limits)

inputs.name: Landslides, Great Britain
inputs.source: BGS National Landslide Database (index)
inputs.licence: Open Government Licence v3 — Contains British Geological Survey materials © UKRI

inputs.name: Landslides, global
inputs.source: NASA Global Landslide Catalog 1997–2016 (data.gov export)
inputs.licence: NASA terms: pending owner confirmation (a US Government work; the data.gov export asks the user to accept NASA's Terms and Conditions, whose text is not published with the catalogue)

inputs.name: Lithology
inputs.source: GLiM v1.0 gridded 0.5° (Hartmann & Moosdorf 2012, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.788537)

inputs.name: Elevation
inputs.source: Terrarium DEM (AWS Open Data)

inputs.name: Satellite land cover
inputs.source: Esri / Impact Observatory Sentinel-2 10 m land cover 2020

inputs.name: Soil
inputs.source: Pelletier et al. 2016 soil and sediment thickness (ORNL DAAC)
inputs.licence: NASA ORNL DAAC: free to use with citation

inputs.name: Rainfall, climate
inputs.source: NOAA CPC Global Unified daily precipitation, 1991–2020 mean

model.grid: 0.1° global lattice, 60°S–84°N (the flood bake's stack + relief + GLiM)

validation.threshold_rule: per region: Youden's J on the OOB votes of the forest trained on the OTHER regions
validation.holdout: leave one region out: 7 of 8 regions each scored by a forest that never saw it
validation.events: inventoried landslides = 1; pseudo-absences (land near the reports, away from any) = 0

great-britain.message: 203 cells held out, too few slides or absences — a score needs 30 of each

americas-north.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

americas-south.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

asia-south.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

oceania.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

asia-east.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

europe.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

africa-middle-east.threshold_rule: Youden on the other regions' OOB votes

validation.auc_rule: mean of the held-out regions' AUCs (each region's scores come from its own forest, so pooling them mixes calibrations; the pooled figure is auc_pooled)

limits: The 0.1° tier is trained on NASA's catalogue alone: with BGS's 18,000 points it learnt Great Britain (the island solid red on the map) rather than ground. Great Britain cannot be scored at 0.1° (too few absences lie 30 km from any report there); the 250 m tier, trained on both inventories, is the product for Great Britain.
Negatives are pseudo-absences: land drawn near the reports but at least ~1 km (fine) / ~30 km (coarse) from any. An unreported slide among them counts against the model.
NASA's catalogue is compiled from news and follows roads and towns; slides in empty mountains are under-represented, and the forest learns some of where people are.
Lithology is GLiM's dominant class per 0.5° cell: a valley of weak shale in a granite cell reads as granite.
Slope at 250 m reads valley sides gentler than at 30 m; relief over ~1 km carries what the cell slope loses.
Rain is the climate only: this is where ground fails, not when.
NASA's export terms are not published with the catalogue; until confirmed, regions other than Great Britain rest on data whose commercial terms are unknown.
maps.membership: preview: free, not part of membership (until the owner confirms NASA's catalogue terms)

maps.name: Landslide susceptibility — Recipe A weighted overlay (superseded)

model.method: Weighted overlay of reclassified factors (1-5), slope-gated, ranked into quantile classes (docs/ni-prototype/methodology.md Recipe A; recipe.mjs)

parameters.lithology: BGS 625k rcs_d scored 1-5 by recipe.mjs lithologyScore()
parameters.land_cover: not used (CORINE not fetched); weights renormalise over the four

inputs.name: Elevation and slope
inputs.source: Terrarium DEM, the flood bake's common grid

inputs.name: Bedrock geology
inputs.source: BGS Geology 625k (OGL; Contains British Geological Survey materials © UKRI)

inputs.name: Rainfall
inputs.source: Met Office HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 annual normals, IDW (OGL)

inputs.name: Drainage
inputs.source: channels draining >= 2 km² on the DEM (recipe.mjs uses OSM waterways)

inputs.name: Landslide inventory
inputs.source: BGS National Landslide Database index (OGL)

model.grid: 900 x 1050 cells of 0.003 x 0.002 deg (~204 m); recipe.mjs ran at 100 m

lithology.why: cells between BGS 625k bedrock polygons at the coast

validation.threshold_rule: class >= 4 (High + Very High, the worst 30% of the ground by quantile construction) is 'predicted landslide'
validation.holdout: spatial: 1413 inventoried slides in Mid and North Wales (north of 51.95 N), ground that played no part in choosing the slope gate or the class rule
validation.events: BGS National Landslide Database, Wales (OGL); absences sampled 1:1 from cells with no record

extra.acceptance_criterion: >= 70% of slides in High + Very High, those classes <= 30% of area

limits: THE RECIPE DOES NOT TRANSFER NORTH. 59% of the Mid/North Wales slides sit on cells under 5° at this grid (stream-bank and coastal slides in Ceredigion and the till cliffs), against 16% in South Wales, so the slope gate -- tuned on South Wales valley sides -- floors most of them. The South Wales figure reproduces the acceptance report; the held-out figure is the one to believe outside it.
The lithology factor barely discriminates in Wales: the Lower Palaeozoic 'MUDSTONE, SILTSTONE AND SANDSTONE' units score 5 under recipe.mjs's /^MUDSTONE/ rule, about three quarters of the land.
Slope at ~210 m reads lower than at 100 m, so fewer cells reach the steep slope classes than in the NI/South Wales runs; the quantile classes are rank-based and absorb most of it.
The inventory is biased to roads, railways and surveyed valleys; absences sampled at random include unrecorded slides.
Drainage proximity here is DEM channels, not the OSM waterways recipe.mjs used.
Northern Ireland itself cannot be scored: GSNI publishes no open inventory (n = 1 in the BGS index).

maps.name: Cyclone risk

model.method: Poisson rate of distinct storms passing within a fixed radius of a point, over complete seasons; p_yr = 1 - exp(-rate)

inputs.name: IBTrACS v04r01 - International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship
inputs.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
inputs.citation: Knapp, K. R., M. C. Kruk, D. H. Levinson, H. J. Diamond, and C. J. Neumann (2010). Bull. Amer. Meteor. Soc., 91, 363-376.

model.grid: variable, 0.25 to 8.0 degrees; a cell subdivides while the rate inside it varies by more than 2% of the global peak. Cell size is display resolution only - the value is measured at a point, so it is comparable between a large cell and a small one.

validation.threshold_rule: predicted when 1 - exp(-rate x 16 yr) >= 0.5, i.e. rate >= 0.04332/yr
validation.holdout: temporal: rates from the 1980-2009 seasons (30), scored against storms of 2010-2025 (16 complete seasons the training never saw)
validation.events: IBTrACS v04r01 storms within 200 km, read from the published grid's own per-season counts (cyclone-risk-years.json)
validation.sample: 25,421 equal-area Fibonacci-lattice points (113 km apart) within 500 km of any ground a storm reached 1980-2025; each takes the published cell it falls in

limits: Per-season counts are cell means: in a coarse (flat) cell a lattice point is called reached when any part of the cell was, which flatters recall there.
Lattice points are spatially autocorrelated (one storm reaches dozens), so n overstates the number of independent tests; read AUC and the rates, not significance.
A 30-season training window is short for the rarest basins' edges; a storm track's year-to-year shift (ENSO, basin activity) is real variance the map cannot know.

maps.name: Seismic risk

model.method: catalogue rate of earthquakes per magnitude band shaking a point at about MMI VI, each event weighted by P(reach >= d) under a log-normal reach; summed over bands

inputs.name: Three catalogues merged: USGS ComCat (M >= 4.5 since 1900) for density and currency, ISC-GEM v12 (1904-2021) joined on ComCat's own contributing ids for homogenised Mw, and GEM GHEC v1.0 (1008-1903) for the pre-instrumental record
inputs.citation: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program (2017), ANSS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat), https://doi.org/10.5066/F7MS3QZH · International Seismological Centre (2025), ISC-GEM Earthquake Catalogue, https://doi.org/10.31905/d808b825 (Storchak et al. 2013, 2015; Di Giacomo et al. 2018) · GEM Foundation (2013), GEM Global Historical Earthquake Catalogue v1.0, https://doi.org/10.13127/ghea/ghec.1.0
inputs.licence: ComCat is US Government public domain. ISC-GEM and GEM GHEC are CC-BY-SA 3.0, so anything derived from them -- these grids included -- is offered under CC-BY-SA 3.0 with the citations above.

model.grid: variable, 0.25 to 8 degrees; a cell subdivides while the band inside it varies by more than 2% of its peak, is empty in part, or spans a whole magnitude unit of largest-on-record. Cell size is display resolution only.

validation.threshold_rule: predicted when 1 - exp(-rate x 20 yr) >= 0.5, i.e. rate >= 0.03466/yr
validation.holdout: temporal: rates re-stamped from events up to 2005 (each band's own completeness window cut there: m5 1964-2005, m6 1930-2005, m7 1900-2005, m8 1900-2005), scored against the 39,428 M>=5 events of 2006-2025
validation.events: the merged ComCat/ISC-GEM record (bake-seismic.py's own columns); a point is reached when a test event lies inside its median damaging-shaking radius, d <= 10^(0.5M - 1.7) km
validation.sample: 200,000 equal-area Fibonacci-lattice points over the whole globe (51 km apart). Stable interiors and open ocean are true negatives the map gets right for free, which inflates accuracy and specificity -- active_ground_only repeats the scores where the training map is non-zero

limits: Isotropic and depth-blind reach: attenuation differs by region and with depth, so a deep or stable-crust event is mis-sized either way.
Twenty test years is short against M7+ recurrence; most positives come from M5-6 events, which is what the score mostly rewards.
Aftershock sequences are not declustered, in training or test: a sequence counts many times, and it recurs where it trained, which flatters the hold-out.
Lattice points are spatially autocorrelated; n is not the number of independent tests.

maps.name: Volcanic risk

model.method: eruptions per year depositing >= 1 mm of ash at a point, each eruption weighted by P(reach >= d) under a log-normal reach per VEI; windows by size class

parameters.stamp: VEI < 5 to R exp(2.0 sigma); VEI >= 5 global

inputs.name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Volcanoes of the World (Holocene eruption catalogue)
inputs.citation: Global Volcanism Program (2024). Volcanoes of the World, v. 5.2. Smithsonian Institution. https://doi.org/10.5479/si.GVP.VOTW5-2024.5.2

model.grid: variable, 0.25 to 8.0 degrees; a cell subdivides while the band inside it varies by more than 2% of its peak, or is empty in part, or spans two largest-VEI classes. Cell size is display resolution only.

validation.threshold_rule: predicted when 1 - exp(-rate x 26 yr) >= 0.5, i.e. rate >= 0.02666/yr
validation.holdout: temporal: rates rebuilt from eruptions up to 1999 (windowed mode; windows small 1950-1999, vei4 1900-1999, vei56 1550-1999, vei7 -9700-1999), scored against the 941 confirmed eruptions of 2000-2025
validation.events: GVP Volcanoes of the World, confirmed eruptions; a point is reached when it lies inside the eruption's median 1 mm ash reach, R by VEI
validation.sample: 141,023 equal-area Fibonacci-lattice points (20 km apart) within 200 km of a catalogue volcano

limits: Isotropic ash: a plume goes downwind, so the reach disc is wrong in shape for every real eruption, and recall/precision read that as misses and false alarms.
An eruption in GVP is an episode: a volcano erupting through the cutoff (Etna, Sakurajima) trains and tests on the same activity, which flatters the hold-out.
The test eruptions are dominated by VEI <= 2, whose reach is a few lattice spacings; most of the map's large-VEI reach is never tested in 26 years.
Lattice points are spatially autocorrelated; n is not the number of independent tests.

maps.name: Volcanic risk (full Holocene record)

model.method: eruptions per year depositing >= 1 mm of ash at a point, each eruption weighted by P(reach >= d) under a log-normal reach per VEI; windows by size class; where a volcano has no eruption of a size inside its window, its own record span

parameters.stamp: VEI < 5 to R exp(2.0 sigma); VEI >= 5 global
